I had a difficulty trying to find home, sit/stand because of the words are small to notice it’s there. 

The 2 options below 3 options are going to be very useless because I don’t want to shop, including the events that are live. 

The new quick menu look does look very useless, with the full menu I prefer the old one. Why I wanna go to live or upcoming events that I’m not interested?

+1 .. Gave it a chance, but the most used buttons like "respawn" and "calibrate" is just .. a lot more inconvenient now.. Like.. why?

Not to mention the content of the big menu (Live now) section being utterly irrelevant to how I use vrc. I could not care less. And even having it automatically pop up on every start is just infuriating. 

I gave it a go. Tried not to judge it. But nothing of these changes have been an improvement - Quite the opposite.

I also think that this Launchpad update is not a good one.

To summarize briefly:

Don't move important buttons too frequently.

Don't make important buttons smaller.

Don't remove the expand button.

Don't leave too much white space.

You should judge the importance of a button based on how many times you press it.

You should carefully align what users need with what the management wants them to use.

Another way to put it is this:The menu from about a year ago is better. 

I thought that criticism alone would only complicate the situation, so I only made the bare minimum changes and created an image as an example of a better design.

I've posted it alongside the current version for easy comparison.

I believe there are many areas that could be improved if we carefully honed them in on them, but I intentionally kept the changes to a minimum.

System overhauls are important at times, but innovation without user support is simply destructive. If the person who created this UI arbitrarily swapped the back and home buttons on the smartphone, and changed the PC keyboard from QWERTY to AZERTY, or vice versa, would people understand how inconvenient it would be?

Very much like the change to Windows 11, UI changes are annoying. I know we'll adjust but the amount of times on muscle memory I accidently misclick when trying to open the social tab or calibrate is insane. Please do not go move the most used buttons on a whim.
